rows.label: Core survey course on Europe (one of the named examples the catalog can match)
rows.note: The page gives five examples and sends students to the program website for the full list. GOVT 3437 and STS 1942 are named only as plain text (no course link, not in the catalog dump), so the checker will not accept them as ids; they are left to the confirm row. This seat is the stricter reading.

rows.label: If your core course is GOVT 3437, STS 1942 or another course on the program's core list, confirm it counts
Show competence in a European language (third-semester course, competency exam, or native speaker)
rows.note: No language courses are named, so the board cannot check this; if you pass the exam or are a native speaker, add one extra course to reach five.

rows.label: Three elective courses on Europe-related topics, in the disciplines the program names
rows.note: Whether a course is about Europe is not something the board can see, and the program keeps the current course list on its website. A course counts only when you answer that it is an approved Europe-related elective, and only if it is in one of the named disciplines (the page says 'including', so a course in another discipline may also be accepted; ask the program and it will not count here). The core course above is used up first and cannot also be an elective.

rows.label: Reach at least five courses in total (up to seven depending on language level)

questions.quote: These electives are courses on more narrowly defined Europe-related topics, in disciplines including: History, Government, Sociology, Anthropology, Comparative Literature, English, Architecture, History of Art and Visual Studies, Classics, Music, Philosophy, Industrial and Labor Relations, Science and Technology Studies.
